# Vault test corpus

Committed fixtures for the unlock corpus (task-7) and the save round-trip
harness (task-8). Real databases written by real KeePass clients, not files
this crate generated — the whole point is to exercise the parsing and
re-serialization paths our own builder would never produce.

## Provenance

Copied verbatim from [`sseemayer/keepass-rs`][upstream] at tag `v0.15.0`
(the exact version `Cargo.lock` pins), `tests/resources/`. Upstream is MIT
licensed (Copyright (c) 2019 Stefan Seemayer); the corpus is redistributed
under that license with this note as attribution.

[upstream]: https://github.com/sseemayer/keepass-rs

`test_db_kdbx41_features.kdbx` is documented upstream as "a real KDBX 4.1
file generated by KeePassXC 2.7.12" — it exists to regression-test the
writer against KeePassXC's own reader, which makes it the anchor fixture
of the round-trip harness.

## Credentials

Every password-protected fixture uses the password `demopass`, with two
exceptions: `test_db_kdbx4_with_totp_entry.kdbx` opens with `test` (it is
exercised by an inline unit test upstream, in `src/db/otp.rs`), and
`test_db_kdbx4_with_keyfile.kdbx` uses no password at all — only
`test_key.key`.

## The corpus

| Fixture | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_password_argon2.kdbx` | KDBX 4, Argon2d, AES |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_password_argon2id.kdbx` | KDBX 4, Argon2id, AES |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_password_argon2id_chacha20.kdbx` | KDBX 4, Argon2id, ChaCha20 |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_password_argon2id_twofish.kdbx` | KDBX 4, Argon2id, Twofish |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_password_argon2_chacha20.kdbx` | KDBX 4, Argon2d, ChaCha20 |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_password_argon2_twofish.kdbx` | KDBX 4, Argon2d, Twofish |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_password_aes.kdbx` | KDBX 4, AES-KDF, AES |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_keyfile.kdbx` + `test_key.key` | KDBX 4, keyfile (raw 32-byte) |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_keyfile_v2.kdbx` + `test_db_kdbx4_with_keyfile_v2.keyx` | KDBX 4, password + XML v2 keyfile |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_password_deleted_entry.kdbx` | KDBX 4, entry in the recycle bin |
| `test_db_kdbx4_with_totp_entry.kdbx` | KDBX 4, TOTP-configured entry |
| `test_db_kdbx41_features.kdbx` | **KDBX 4.1, authored by KeePassXC 2.7.12** |
| `test_db_kdbx41_with_password_aes.kdbx` | KDBX 4.1, AES |
| `test_db_with_password.kdbx` | KDBX 3.1 — read-compat; save must refuse |

The KDBX 3.1 fixture is here on purpose: reading it must work (§1 of the
save policy), and saving it must *fail* — the on-disk format is KDBX 4
(decision-3), and the round-trip harness proves the refusal leaves the
original byte-identical.
